fields.expected:
The most relevant thing I've built for a developer-productivity role is a local browser automation agent for job applications. The problem was that job hunting is mostly repetitive browser work, but a fully autonomous browser agent is dangerous there: one wrong action submits a real application or fabricates an answer. So I built it in TypeScript and Node with Playwright, using SQLite as the single source of truth because automation gets unsafe when application state can diverge across processes. Every application moves through an explicit state machine (DISCOVERED through SUBMITTED), every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED that never default on, and free-text and demographic fields are architecturally blocked from auto-fill and always route to human review. I also built a validation ladder from unit-confirmed to live-mutation-confirmed, so nothing counts as working just because it passed against a fixture. I built an operator console on top of it for running and approving the pipeline.

That is the part of internal tooling and AI agents I would want to work on at Bear: making the boundary between machine action and human judgment explicit so engineers actually trust the automation. I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins and available onsite in Redwood City.
